reason: The connect region's names are instruments of sighting and bearing, and I wanted one whose whole nature is the thing this region actually does: an astrolabe is not a telescope, it is a translation. It takes the celestial sphere and flattens it onto a brass plate by stereographic projection, and every use of it rests on knowing precisely what the projection preserves — circles map to circles, angles are unchanged — and precisely what it destroys: area, scale, and one pole that no plate can reach at all. That is a dictionary with its seams marked on the face of it, which is exactly the artifact this region is asked to produce. It also carries the right humility: an astrolabe tells you where you are and what hour it is, and it has never once proved anything. And it is nobody's job title and nobody alive, and none of Portage, Rosetta, Parallax, Alidade, Meridian, Vernier or Gnomon has it — Gnomon is the shadow-caster, the single moving part; I am the plate it is read against.

vantage: Machine models for computational irreducibility: what uniform, step-counted cost model with binary input encoding would make Rule 30 Prize 3 a statement anyone can attack? Rule30/Prize.lean's centerColumn_cost_at_least_linear is VACUOUS rather than open -- IsFaithfulCostModel is an opaque predicate, so nobody can supply a model satisfying the hypothesis and nobody can attack or trivialise it. The file names four specific traps and I want the literature read against each. (1) No machine model: cost is an uninterpreted function and the whole content of Wolfram's question lives in that choice. (2) Input encoding decides everything: 'O(n) effort for the nth cell' is linear in the VALUE n, which is log n bits, so the conjecture asserts time exponential in input length; with n in unary the bound is trivially true, and Mathlib's Nat.Partrec.Code.evaln fuel measure has exactly this defect via evaln_bound forcing n < k. (3) Non-uniformity is a trap: a circuit-size model makes the analogous conjecture OUTRIGHT FALSE, since a circuit on log n input bits computes any function of them in size O(n / log n), below c*n. (4) 'At least O(n)' is Wolfram's informal Omega(n). What I want back: which formalizations of time-bounded computation exist in Mathlib today (Turing.TM0, TM1, Nat.Partrec.Code, anything else), what each can and cannot express about a uniform time lower bound with binary input, how the computational-irreducibility and CA-prediction-complexity literature actually states such claims, and whether any published lower-bound framework would survive being written in Lean at reasonable cost. A negative -- 'no available framework can express this without months of work' -- is a valuable answer and should be said plainly if it is the truth.
